author: Sean9henry
text:
It seems that everybody has been quiet recently. So I put up a PAZ topic to wake people up

PAZ seems to be the term that confused many along their learning path. I
 have come to the understanding that PAZ is basically all price zones,
which can be further divided into mainly pole PAZ and compression PAZ,
these two are potentially tradable given a proper setup and favorable
R/R ratio, the other non-tradable PAZ is the flag formed by FTRs,
supplies, demands, and S/W flip zones, where they are too narrow to
have proper setups and favorable R/R ratio.

I have marked my understanding in the chart below. Can anyone comment or
 confirm? Of course if the Master has time to honor us, I will be
extremely delighted !

I also have other observations marked, please kindly critique if
anything is off. Thanks and have a great weekend wherever you are!

Sean.

author: Ifmyante
text:
In response to a pm I got this morning:

Lately I had a man-cold, and for a while during that time I'd open the chart and feel I had no idea what I was looking at.

I knew I knew the market, but there was still something inside me telling me that I wouldn't be able to read it

This wasn't upsetting at all , because I knew full well this malady would pass and I'd be back on top of it again.

This can happen to anybody, due to illness, fatigue, fear of failure, fear of success, or any number of other causes.

For a student this can be very distressing and debilitating.

But it need not be terminal. The problem is not that one's read has
gone. The loss of the read is just a manifestation of another problem in
 life.

That's why, when we lose it, we must step away from the charts, and look within ourselves to find the unresolved issues.

Once we've faced and fixed them, we can get straight back to work in a
better state than if we never had the problem in the first place

I remember when I was learning the market, I'd have these EUREKA moments, which were wonderful!

I'd think to myself "I've got it! I've got it!" and imagine that now everything I did would be perfect from then on.

But it wasn't. I'd still not be right all the time. Soon I'd get another eureka moment, and think I had it again. But no.

There are a number of lessons which need to be learned, and each helps.
After all these lessons are learned, it still takes time for them all to
 fit together.

Once they do all come together, we don't think "EUREKA". Instead we sigh, and say "I'm ready".

author: Sean9henry
text:
Hi IF,

After a lot of reading from this great site, I have come to a relatively
 clear thought of the concept behind the RTM way of trading. The only
thing is, I am not affirmative of it yet. I would really appreciate it
if you could help clear it up for me or comment on my thinking !

This is what I think ---

1. Use the s/d, s/r flip, ftr, etc. to identify the potential and high probability price reversal regions in a HTF.

2. As price returns to these identified zones, we switch to a LTF to
see how price reacts. In the selected LTF, after price trades to the
zone from Step 1, we wait for price to go back down or up to engulf a
significant demand or supply formed before price reached the zone, or
use the various other reaction price patterns discussed to confirm IT's
intention of taking price down or up.

3. Then, as price returns to a supply or demand formed at or near the
zone identified in Step 1, a touch trade or confirmed trade can be
taken.

4. Place the stop beyond the edge of the zone identified in Step 1;
target 1 is the next demand or supply in the LTF used, while the final
target is the original of the move to the zone identified in Step 1,
often the next demand or supply in that HTF used.

The reason you wanted us to put the puzzle pieces together instead of
handing over the golden keys is for us to accumulate the chart
experiences (screen hours), and figure out what HTF and LTF would work,
and to form the psychology to follow the plan.

Many many thanks!

Sean.

author: Sean9henry
text:
The Arizona Department of Safety Officer pulled over pick-up truck
owner Mike Murray for a weapons check because of an NRA bumper sticker.
When the officer approached the vehicle, the man behind the wheel handed
 the officer his driver's license, insurance card and concealed carry
permit. The officer took all the documents, looked them over and said,
"Mr. Murray, I see you have a CCP. Do you have any weapons with you?"
The driver replied, "Yes I do. I have a 357 handgun in a hip holster, a
.45 in the glove box and a .22 derringer in my boot." The officer looked
 at Mike and asked, "Anything else?" "Yes. I have a Mossberg 500 12
gauge and an AR-15 in the trunk." The officer asked if the man was
driving to or from a shooting range and the man said he wasn't, so the
officer bent over and looked into the driver's face and said "Mr.
Murray, you're carrying quite a few guns. May I ask what you are afraid
of?" Mike locked eyes with the officer and calmly answered, "Not a
fucking thing."

Courtesy from the internet...
